title: Make the captioning API image rebuild in seconds
context: Your pod issue is "Containerise the captioning API with Docker". Right now every one-line code change reinstalls PyTorch, the image is over 1 GB and the API runs as root. Fix the Dockerfile before Priya reviews it.
prompt:
Rewrite this Dockerfile so that:
1. Changing a line of app code doesn't reinstall the dependencies.
2. The image starts from a smaller official Python base.
3. The API doesn't run as root.
4. pip doesn't leave its download cache in the image.
Keep the API serving on port 8000.
starter:
FROM python:3.12
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

rubric.title: Dependencies install in their own cached layer
rubric.description: requirements.txt is copied and installed before the rest of the source.
rubric.hint: When you change one line in app/main.py, which layers does Docker rebuild? Where does pip install sit relative to the step that copies your code?

rubric.title: Starts from a smaller base image
rubric.description: The base image ships only what the API needs.
rubric.hint: What does the full python:3.12 image include that a web API never uses, like compilers and docs? Does the official image come in a smaller variant?

rubric.title: Runs as a non-root user
rubric.description: The last USER instruction switches away from root.
rubric.hint: If someone found a bug in your API and got a shell in the container, which user would they be? Which instruction decides that?

rubric.title: Leaves no pip cache behind
rubric.description: Downloaded wheels aren't kept in the image layer.
rubric.hint: After pip installs a package, does the image still need the file it downloaded? Is there a pip option or environment variable about its cache?

checks.title: uvicorn listens on 0.0.0.0:8000
checks.description: The API is reachable from outside the container.
checks.hint: If uvicorn listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container, can your laptop reach it through the published port?

checks.title: CMD uses the exec form
checks.description: The start command is a JSON array, so stop signals reach uvicorn.
checks.hint: When you stop the container, which process receives the signal if CMD is a plain string?

checks.title: Sets a working directory
checks.description: Paths in COPY and CMD resolve against a known folder.
checks.hint: Without a WORKDIR, where do relative paths like app.main end up?

sampleAnswer:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY --chown=app:app . .
USER app
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

resources.title: Docker docs: Optimise builds with the build cache

title: Caption 64 images in one forward pass
context: The pod's issue "Add PyTorch batch inference" needs the API to handle a batch of uploads. The current helper runs the model once per image, tracks gradients it never uses and returns CUDA tensors FastAPI can't serialise.
prompt:
Rewrite predict_batch so that it:
1. Puts the model in inference behaviour (dropout and batch norm off).
2. Doesn't build an autograd graph while predicting.
3. Sends all images through the model in one batched forward pass.
4. Runs on whatever device it's given.
It must still return a list of predicted class ids.
starter:
import torch


def predict_batch(model, images, device="cpu"):
    """images: a list of 3x224x224 float tensors. Return a list of predicted class ids."""
    preds = []
    for img in images:
        out = model(img)
        preds.append(out.argmax())
    return preds

rubric.title: Switches the model to evaluation mode
rubric.description: Dropout and batch norm behave as they do at inference time.
rubric.hint: Dropout randomly zeroes activations while training. How do you tell a PyTorch module you're only predicting now?

rubric.title: Doesn't track gradients
rubric.description: Prediction runs without building an autograd graph.
rubric.hint: Does prediction ever call backward()? What is autograd storing for all 64 images, and is there a context that turns it off?

rubric.title: One batched forward pass
rubric.description: The images become one [N, 3, 224, 224] tensor before the model sees them.
rubric.hint: What shape does one image have, and what shape does the model expect? How could you combine N tensors into one along a new first dimension?

rubric.title: Model and batch share a device
rubric.description: Both the model and the input move to the device argument.
rubric.hint: If the model's weights are on the GPU and the batch is on the CPU, what happens on the forward pass? Which method moves a tensor or a module?

checks.title: Keeps the predict_batch(model, images, device) signature
checks.description: Callers in the API don't need to change.
checks.hint: The FastAPI route calls predict_batch(model, images, device=...). Does your function still accept those arguments?

checks.title: Takes argmax over the class dimension
checks.description: One prediction per image, not one for the whole batch.
checks.hint: For a [N, classes] tensor, what does argmax() return when you don't name a dimension?

checks.title: Returns values the API can serialise
checks.description: Plain Python numbers or a CPU tensor, not a CUDA tensor.
checks.hint: Can FastAPI turn a CUDA tensor into JSON? What would you call to get plain Python numbers?

sampleAnswer:
import torch


def predict_batch(model, images, device="cpu"):
    """images: a list of 3x224x224 float tensors. Return a list of predicted class ids."""
    model.eval()
    model.to(device)
    batch = torch.stack(images).to(device)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        logits = model(batch)
    return logits.argmax(dim=1).cpu().tolist()

resources.title: PyTorch tutorial: Saving and loading models for inference

title: Who uses the captioning API most?
context: Tom designed the Postgres schema for caption requests. The pod wants a weekly report of heavy users, and the first draft returns millions of rows because it cross-joins two tables.
prompt:
Write one query that returns, for each user with at least 3 completed requests in the last 7 days: their user_id, how many completed requests they made, and the average caption confidence. Busiest users first.

Tables:
  caption_requests(id, user_id, image_url, status, created_at)
  captions(id, request_id, text, confidence, created_at)
starter:
-- caption_requests(id, user_id, image_url, status, created_at)
-- captions(id, request_id, text, confidence, created_at)
SELECT user_id, confidence
FROM caption_requests, captions;

rubric.title: Joins captions to their request
rubric.description: An explicit JOIN on the key that links the two tables.
rubric.hint: With 10 requests and 10 captions and no join condition, how many rows come back? Which column in captions points at a request?

rubric.title: Filters rows before grouping
rubric.description: Only completed requests from the last 7 days are counted.
rubric.hint: Which rows should be thrown away before you count anything? How would you say "the last 7 days" relative to now, so the report stays right next week?

rubric.title: One row per user, summarised
rubric.description: Grouped by user, with a count and an average.
rubric.hint: You want one row per user. Which clause collapses many rows into one, and which functions summarise a group?

rubric.title: Filters groups after counting
rubric.description: Users with fewer than 3 completed requests are left out.
rubric.hint: Can WHERE see the result of COUNT? Which clause filters after the groups exist?

checks.title: Returns user_id
checks.description: The report says who each row is about.
checks.hint: Which column tells the pod who each row is about?

checks.title: Busiest users first
checks.hint: In what order do rows come back if you don't ask for one?

checks.title: Names its columns
checks.description: No SELECT *, so the report doesn't change when the schema does.
checks.hint: What happens to this report when someone adds a column to caption_requests?

sampleAnswer:
SELECT r.user_id,
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) AS completed_requests,
       ROUND(AVG(c.confidence)::numeric, 2) AS avg_confidence
FROM caption_requests r
JOIN captions c ON c.request_id = r.id
WHERE r.status = 'completed'
  AND r.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY r.user_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.id) >= 3
ORDER BY completed_requests DESC;

title: Give the captioning API only the access it needs
context: Priya is deploying the API to AWS. It reads uploads from s3://visionaid-uploads/incoming/ and writes captions to s3://visionaid-captions/. The draft IAM policy lets it do anything to every bucket in the account.
prompt:
Rewrite the IAM policy with least privilege:
1. The API can read objects only under visionaid-uploads/incoming/.
2. It can write objects only to visionaid-captions.
3. No wildcard actions and no account-wide resources.
It must stay valid JSON.

rubric.title: Names each action
rubric.description: No s3:* or * actions.
rubric.hint: If this role's keys leaked, what could someone do with s3:*? Which S3 calls does a captioning API actually make?

rubric.title: Reads only where uploads land
rubric.description: GetObject, scoped to the incoming/ prefix.
rubric.hint: Which bucket and which folder does the API read from? Can a Resource ARN name a prefix inside a bucket?

rubric.title: Writes only captions
rubric.description: PutObject, scoped to the captions bucket.
rubric.hint: Where should captions go, and does the API need to write anywhere else?

rubric.title: No account-wide resources
rubric.description: Every statement names its bucket.
rubric.hint: What does "Resource": "*" include that this API never touches?

checks.title: Is valid JSON
checks.hint: Paste it into a JSON validator in your head: are all commas and brackets where they should be?

checks.title: Uses policy language 2012-10-17
checks.hint: IAM has two policy language versions. Which one supports policy variables?

checks.title: Never deletes user uploads
checks.hint: Does a captioning service ever need to delete what a user uploaded?

title: Make the image loader safe to call 1,000 times
context: Mei's preprocessing module loads every upload through load_image. Under load the API runs out of file handles, transparent PNGs break the model, and a PDF upload crashes the worker with a stack trace.
prompt:
Improve load_image so that it:
1. Always closes the file, even when resizing fails.
2. Returns a 3-channel RGB image whatever the upload's colour mode.
3. Turns unreadable files into a clear ValueError the API can show the user.
4. Has type hints, so teammates know what goes in and what comes out.
starter:
from PIL import Image


def load_image(path, size=224):
    img = Image.open(path)
    img = img.resize((size, size))
    return img

rubric.title: Closes the file every time
rubric.description: The image is opened in a context manager.
rubric.hint: After 1,000 calls, how many file handles are still open? Which Python statement guarantees cleanup even when an exception is raised halfway?

rubric.title: Normalises the colour mode
rubric.description: Every image comes out as RGB.
rubric.hint: A transparent PNG has 4 channels and a scanned page may have 1. How many does the model expect, and can Pillow change an image's mode?

rubric.title: Fails with a clear message
rubric.description: Unreadable files raise ValueError with a readable reason.
rubric.hint: What does Pillow raise today when someone uploads a PDF? What would you want the API to tell that person instead?

rubric.title: Typed signature
rubric.description: Parameters and the return value have type hints.
rubric.hint: How would a teammate know what load_image returns without reading its body?

checks.title: Keeps load_image(path, size=224)
checks.description: The rest of the pipeline still calls it the same way.
checks.hint: Does the function the API imports still exist with the same name and default size?

checks.title: Returns the image
checks.description: Every successful path returns a value.
checks.hint: What does the caller receive if the function reaches its end without a return?

checks.title: Raises instead of printing
checks.description: Errors reach the API, not the server log.
checks.hint: If the function prints a warning and carries on, what does the API send back to the user?

title: Ship your Dockerfile as a clean pull request
context: You're on main with a new Dockerfile and a .env file that holds the pod's API key. The commands below would push the key to GitHub, straight onto main, with the message "stuff".
prompt:
Write the git commands, one per line, to:
1. Start from an up-to-date main.
2. Do the work on a new branch.
3. Commit only the Dockerfile (never .env) with a message that says what changed.
4. Push the branch so you can open a pull request for Priya to review.
starter:
git add .
git commit -m "stuff"
git push

rubric.title: Works on a branch
rubric.description: A new branch for the change, not main.
rubric.hint: If you push straight to main, when does Priya get to review your work?

rubric.title: Stages only what belongs in the PR
rubric.description: The Dockerfile is added by name.
rubric.hint: What does `git add .` pick up besides your Dockerfile? What's inside .env?

rubric.title: The message says what changed
rubric.description: A commit message a teammate understands in six weeks.
rubric.hint: Six weeks from now, what will "stuff" tell Mei about this commit?

rubric.title: Pushes the branch with an upstream
rubric.description: The first push says where the branch goes.
rubric.hint: The first time you push a new branch, how does Git know which remote branch it should track?

checks.title: Never stages .env
checks.hint: Which file in your folder must never reach GitHub?

checks.title: Starts from the latest main
checks.hint: If main moved while you worked, where does your branch start from?

checks.title: Commits before pushing
checks.hint: What does git push send if nothing has been committed yet?

sampleAnswer:
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/dockerise-api
echo ".env" >> .gitignore
git add Dockerfile .gitignore
git commit -m "Add a Dockerfile for the captioning API"
git push -u origin feat/dockerise-api

resources.title: Pro Git book: Basic branching and merging
